In a DW Business interview , he argues that Europe should concentrate on building technologies other countries need, with robots taking on physical work in factories and eventually homes.

title: New ISO interoperability standard covers collaboration among mobile robots from multiple vendors
summary: The ISO 21423:2026 interoperability standard is intended to allow mobile robots from multiple vendors to communicate and coordinate.
points: The new ISO 21423:2026 standard is intended to facilitate communications among different mobile robots.

The Association for Advancing Automation, or A3, yesterday published ISO 21423:2026, a new international standard for communications among industrial mobile robots, or IMRs, regardless of vendor or model.
“Companies want to choose the robots that fit their applications and have those robots work together on the same floor,” stated Carole Franklin, director of standards development for robotics at A3.

A cumulative working-time counter tracks progress through the shift, while overlays label the footage autonomous and show playback speeds including 5x and 100x.

A practical example involving Cooltrax brings these benefits to life.

title: Ceva and Mobilint advance Physical AI with REGULUS edge AI SoC
summary: Mobilint has deployed Ceva's SensPro AI DSP and NeuPro-Nano NPU in its REGULUS edge AI SoC, delivering 10 TOPS at under 3W for Physical AI devices.
points: As AI becomes embedded across the physical world, workloads are increasingly being processed where they can run most effectively and efficiently, from the cloud to the device itself.
For Physical AI systems that must sense, interpret and respond to their surroundings in real time, this is driving greater intelligence directly into power-constrained edge devices.
Designed as a standalone processor for on-device AI , REGULUS integrates Ceva’s SensPro AI DSP and NeuPro-Nano NPN32 NPU within Mobilint’s highly integrated processing architecture.

“It’s not only that Tutor’s models let robots do jobs that robots have never been able to do before,” stated Josh Gruenstein, co-founder and CEO of Tutor Intelligence.

summary: ThermAffyx addresses secure positioning and heating of patients for robot-assisted surgical procedures with a minimal OR footprint.
points: ThermAffyx both securely positions and warms patients during robot-assisted surgeries.
Many healthcare advances come from within that industry, but innovations from other industries can also find a role.
Gentherm Medical has designed its ThermAffyx Patient Safety System based on thermal management experience from the automotive industry.

title: Humanoid Robot Batteries Could Become an $850 Million Market by 2037, IDTechEx Forecasts
summary: IDTechEx forecasts an $850 million humanoid battery market by 2037, as manufacturers pursue fast charging, battery swapping and new chemistries to extend working time.
points: The market for humanoid robot batteries could reach US$850 million by 2037, according to IDTechEx’s public overview of its new battery report .
The research firm projects a ten-year compound annual growth rate of 34.2%, with battery swapping contributing to demand for additional packs.
The report examines batteries for industrial, commercial and domestic humanoids.

summary: Brett Adcock shares newly manufactured Figure 03 robots walking across campus from BotQ, offering a glimpse of the fleet without new production or delivery figures.
points: Brett Adcock has shared a short video of newly manufactured Figure 03 humanoids leaving BotQ and walking across Figure’s campus, offering a glimpse of the company’s growing robot fleet outside the factory.
“Newly manufactured F.03 robots leaving BotQ and heading across campus,” the Figure founder and CEO wrote in his November 2 post on X .
The roughly 19-second video shows the white-and-black robots making their way along the approach to the building, with one moving across the painted pedestrian crossing as others follow behind.

title: Muscle coordination can be mimicked by electric motors – it could lead to improved robots
summary: Coordination appears to emerge spontaneously from muscle fibres.
points: They pick up a bag, tighten a grip, climb a hill, hold a cup of coffee and the body quietly adjusts force, speed and position without the person ever thinking about it.
It is able to produce force smoothly and reliably, even though it is built from huge numbers of tiny molecular components.
When the load changes, muscles don’t simply wobble or fail.

title: DEEP Robotics Humanoids Join Traffic Police at Hangzhou Marathon
summary: Hangxing No.2 humanoids based on DEEP Robotics’ DR02 platform supported traffic operations around Huanglong Sports Center during the November 1 race.
points: DEEP Robotics’ humanoids joined traffic-management operations at the Hangzhou Marathon on November 1, taking on a supporting role around the city’s Huanglong Sports Center.

title: AT&T and Smart Meter expand connected healthcare reach with Global SIM Advanced
summary: AT&T and Smart Meter are expanding their collaboration, using AT&T Global SIM Advanced multi-profile eSIM to keep cellular remote patient monitoring devices connected in more locations across the US.
points: AT&T and Smart Meter are expanding their collaboration aimed at helping healthcare providers maintain connectivity for remote patient monitoring devices in more locations across the United States.

As healthcare organisations increasingly rely on connected technologies to support patients managing chronic conditions outside traditional care settings, consistent connectivity remains essential to delivering timely health insights.

Smart Meter is a provider of cellular-enabled remote patient monitoring (RPM), helping healthcare organisations remotely track key health indicators such as glucose levels, blood pressure, weight and oxygen saturation.

title: Lightberry’s Lumi Gains Conditional FCC Covered List Exemption
summary: CEO Ali Attar tells Humanoids Daily that Lumi’s exemption clears the way to apply for FCC certification, with shipments expected “very soon” but no firm date.
points: Lightberry’s Lumi has received a conditional exemption from the Federal Communications Commission’s Covered List, giving the Unitree-based humanoid a specific regulatory clearance tied to a plan to move manufacturing to the United States.
CEO Ali Attar told Humanoids Daily that the exemption allows Lightberry to apply for independent FCC certification, a further step before off-the-shelf customer sales.
The FCC’s October 30 public notice explicitly names Lightberry Holdings’ Lumi interactive mobile robots among devices granted Conditional Approval by the U.S.

title: 1X Teammates Use Spare NEO Heads to Test Home Integrations, Starting With the TV
summary: A clip shared by Dar Sleeper shows a NEO head called Dexter choosing and playing The Lord of the Rings on a TV as teammates test home integrations.
points: A NEO head perched on a living-room mantelpiece is getting a head start on home integration—by choosing a film and putting it on the television.
In a 41-second clip shared by 1X’s Dar Sleeper , a man addresses the head as “Dexter” and asks it to pick something to watch.
The TV wakes, navigates a TV interface and begins playing The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring .

title: AGIBOT Livestreams Six G2 Robots in a 24-Hour Convenience Store Challenge
summary: Six G2 robots face rush-hour service, overnight duty and breakfast preparation in AGIBOT’s November 2–3 livestreamed store challenge.
points: AGIBOT is putting six G2 robots through a convenience-store shift in a 24-hour livestream, offering viewers an extended look at its machines working around people, shelves and service counters.
The company’s “Robots Never Clock Out” challenge runs from November 2 at 10:00 a.m. to November 3 at 10:00 a.m.
That is 02:00 UTC to 02:00 UTC , or 03:00 CET to 03:00 CET , on the same dates.

title: 28 Zero-Day Findings in Less Than Two Days: What AI-Speed Discovery Means for Robotics
summary: VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem.
points: These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.
